prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core theme: Secure a strong economy to fund public services and improve life at every stage.

Economy, tax and infrastructure
- Eliminate the deficit, run a surplus, and keep debt falling; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance.
- Raise Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40% threshold to £50,000; crack down on tax avoidance/evasion.
- Invest £100bn+ in infrastructure: HS2/HS3, rail electrification, Crossrail 2, £15bn for roads, cycling, and greener vehicles.
- Freeze regulated commuter rail fares; roll out 95% superfast broadband by 2017, improve mobile coverage and 5G.
- Drive regional growth (Northern Powerhouse, Midlands Engine); devolve powers and budgets to city regions with elected mayors.

Jobs, business and skills
- Create 2 million more jobs and 3 million new apprenticeships; aim for full employment.
- Youth policy: time‑limited Youth Allowance (18–21), work/learning requirements; restrict Housing Benefit for 18–21s.
- Cut £10bn more red tape; review business rates; boost exports and SME procurement; permanent Office of Tax Simplification.
- Halve the disability employment gap; require big firms to publish gender pay gaps.

Welfare and family
- “Tax‑Free Minimum Wage” law so 30 hours on the NMW pays no Income Tax; keep overall welfare cap.
- Lower household benefit cap to £23,000; freeze working‑age benefits for two years (key exemptions); roll out Universal Credit.
- Childcare: 30 hours free for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds; tax‑free childcare; support for marriage/civil partnerships.

Housing
- Double first‑time buyers; extend Help to Buy and launch Help to Buy ISA (25% top‑up).
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount) for under‑40s; 275,000 additional affordable homes; prioritise brownfield.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; protect the Green Belt.

Education and training
- Protect per‑pupil funding; tough literacy/numeracy standards and core academic GCSEs (EBacc).
- Turn failing/coasting schools into academies; open 500 new free schools; recruit 17,500 extra maths/physics teachers.
- Expand UTCs and degree apprenticeships; abolish cap on university places; introduce postgraduate loans.

NHS and social care
- Increase NHS spending by at least £8bn by 2020; deliver a 7‑day NHS and GP access (same‑day for over‑75s).
- Integrate health and social care (Better Care Fund); enhance cancer care, mental health access standards, and dementia strategy.
- Cap residential social care costs; expand primary care and prevention.

Immigration
- Net migration target in the tens of thousands; reform EU welfare (four‑year residency before in‑work benefits; no child benefits for children abroad).
- End jobseeker benefits for EU migrants; stronger removals, exit checks, landlord checks; tackle illegal working; Controlling Migration Fund.

Crime, justice and extremism
- Complete police reform; boost cyber capability; ban new psychoactive substances; sobriety orders.
- Modernise prisons and rehabilitation; Victims’ Law; stronger action on VAWG and child exploitation.
- Scrap the Human Rights Act; introduce a British Bill of Rights.
- Counter‑terrorism: update communications data powers; new bans and disruption orders for extremist groups/individuals.

Energy and environment
- Lower bills via competition and smart meters; back nuclear, gas and shale; end new subsidies for onshore wind.
- Meet climate targets cost‑effectively; protect countryside and Green Belt; plant 11m trees; major flood defences; create a global “Blue Belt” of marine reserves.

Pensions and older people
- Keep the triple lock; introduce single‑tier pension; protect bus passes, TV licences and Winter Fuel Payments (with temperature test for expats).
- Raise effective Inheritance Tax threshold on main residence to £1m for couples; greater freedom over pension savings and tax‑free inheritance.

Union, Europe, defence and foreign policy
- English votes for English laws; implement new powers for Scotland and Wales; sustain Northern Ireland settlement.
- EU in/out referendum by end of 2017; keep the pound; seek EU reform and repatriation of powers.
- Maintain Armed Forces (Army ≥82,000), renew Trident, invest £160bn in equipment; meet NATO targets.
- Keep aid at 0.7% GNI; focus on poverty, stability, health, and women’s rights.
